strategyPosture: Stay selective into the midday tape: SPY is -0.4% from its high with loose credit (SLOOS 0%), but high rates (10y 5.24%) and narrow rotation argue against chasing extended 1m leaders; the screened work is in DATA_AHEAD dislocations like AVGO, APP, NOW and NXT, sized only after thesis verification.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real rotation, not a confirmed rollover, because credit remains loose - but leadership is narrow and small caps are not confirming. Treat index strength as selective, not broad permission to add.
themes.dataAnchor: Market concentration reads ROTATION_NOT_ROLLOVER: Mag7 averages -9.33% from its 52-week high, a -8.93-point gap to SPY, with TSLA weakest at -23.3% and AAPL strongest at -2.5%. Bank lending standards are LOOSE at SLOOS 0%, well below the ~40% stress threshold, while IWM lags at -3.09% 1m and -6.2% 3m despite SPY +2.74% 1m and QQQ +6.02% 1m.
themes.label: Index Rotation, Not Rollover
themes.narrative: Index-level calm implies broad health, with SPY at 778.57 (+0.6% on the day, +2.74% 1m) only -0.4% from its 52-week high.
themes.watchFor: SLOOS moving toward 40% or the Mag7-vs-SPY gap widening beyond -8.93 points would change the rotation read.

themes.counterRead: Price is running ahead of the rate data: tight credit and a falling VIX are supporting equities while nominal and real yields stay elevated. A hot CPI print would test that calm directly, so equity complacency is the risk, not credit stress today.
themes.dataAnchor: Rates are not low: DGS10 is 5.24%, DGS30 is 5.6%, DGS2 is 4.77%, the 2s10s curve is 0.47 and the real 10y is 2.89%, with fed funds (DFF) at 3.88% and breakevens (T10YIE) at 2.35%. HY OAS is tight at 3.09%, and the Sep CPI event on 2026-10-14 is flagged HIGH signal strength, as is the Oct 27-28 FOMC (6 hits).
themes.label: High Rates, Calm Equities Ahead of CPI/FOMC
themes.narrative: Equities and volatility imply the rate backdrop is manageable, with VIX at 14.84 (-3.7% on the day, -16.82% 1m) and QQQ +6.02% 1m.
themes.watchFor: The Oct 14 CPI print and whether DGS10 holds above 5.24% or HY OAS widens materially from 3.09% would change this read.

themes.counterRead: Fundamentals are ahead of price here: the pullback posture across 24 dislocations is RESEARCH_SCREENED - all candidates passed 5-gate screening, verify thesis before sizing. This is the opportunity side of the rotation, rather than chasing the 1m leaders.
themes.dataAnchor: AVGO is top conviction at score 81, Tier A, -27% from its high with revenue +55% YoY, 67.8% gross margin and $26,914M FCF (42.1% margin). APP is -62.5% from its high (RSI 35.4, score 77) with revenue +16.4% YoY in conviction and a watchlist promotion at score 70 citing 55.8% growth, NOW is -27% with revenue +23.1% YoY, and NXT is -47.2% with revenue +20.3% YoY in conviction and 31.6% cited in its promotion thesis; all four promotions are flagged RECOVERY.

themes.narrative: The tape has left former growth leaders for dead, pricing APP, AVGO, NOW and NXT as broken stories rather than recovering businesses.
themes.watchFor: A promotion from watchlist to conviction, or AVGO/APP/NOW/NXT reclaiming trend with RSI holding above 50, would confirm the data-ahead read.

themes.counterRead: The market is paying for operating power and infrastructure exposure and discounting speculative nuclear names. A blanket AI-power narrative is ahead of that split - own the distinction, not the theme label.
themes.dataAnchor: They are diverging: VST is +9.5% 1m (still -25.6% from its high, RSI 64.4, live price 161.48), while SMR is -29.58% 1m, OKLO -13.04% 1m and URA -13.8% 1m. ASTS is -14.99% 1m and -10.54% on the day, in the same speculative laggard group, while PWR is +14.1% 1m and GEV +8.57% 1m among leaders.
themes.label: AI Power Bifurcation
themes.narrative: The AI-power narrative treats operating power and pre-commercial nuclear as one trade.
themes.watchFor: SMR or OKLO reversing their 1m declines of -29.58% and -13.04% while VST holds near 161.48 would challenge the bifurcation read.

themes.counterRead: Without a data anchor in this input to support the pace, these moves are narrative ahead of verified fundamentals. They confirm risk appetite alongside VIX at 14.84, but they are not the screened opportunity - that sits in the dislocated names.
themes.dataAnchor: PLTR is +25.8% 1m and +4.97% on the day, PWR +14.1% 1m, HIMS +12.72% 1m and +10.23% on the day, and META +11.36% 1m. SPY by comparison is +2.74% 1m, so leadership is running roughly 4-9x the index pace with no fundamental anchor for these names in this input.
